engine.policy: default (Q1 doc-example and Q2 splitter-boundary promotions enabled)

purpose: Measure, honestly, whether BDE can discover real historical defects from permitted repository evidence alone (no hand-authored acceptance contracts), and quantify mutation sensitivity and false positives on known-valid code.

track_a.corpus: the frozen v0.2.0 corpus TARGETS ONLY (project, module, fix_commit); the v0.2.0 requirements/contracts/prompts are NOT inputs to BDE at any point

scoring_rubric.DISCOVERED_DEFECT: law fails at baseline AND passes at the upstream fix (witness reproduces the historical defect)
scoring_rubric.TRUE_DOC_DRIFT: fails at both revisions; documented example verifiably contradicts the code (audited; commands in report)
scoring_rubric.TRUE_DELAYED_FIX: fails at both revisions; upstream later changed exactly this behaviour (audited against a later commit)
scoring_rubric.FALSE_POSITIVE: fails at both revisions with no audit support

audit_evidence.isScriptProtocol: tsx -e 'import {isScriptProtocol} from "./src/index.ts"; console.log(isScriptProtocol("javascript:alert(1)"))' -> false, while README/JSDoc document `// true`
audit_evidence.normalizeURL: README documents 'test?query=123%20123#hash,%20test'; the code returns 'test?query=123+123#hash,%20test' (space -> + vs %20)
audit_evidence.withFragment: README documents withFragment('/foo#bar', '') -> '/foo'; the code returns '/foo#bar' (empty hash does not remove the fragment)
audit_evidence.splitByCase: at 9927800 splitByCase('a-', []) -> ['a','-']; at 57cfd15 the same call -> ['a-'] (upstream changed caseless-char handling)

track_b.subjects: the six fix revisions (known-valid) + harmless-refactor controls
track_b.semantics: a surviving mutation is limited detection sensitivity, never a defect claim; refactor controls must produce zero findings

no_post_hoc_changes: the corpus, rubric and audit labels are frozen before the formal run; results are published as measured
